content.title: KITCHEN FIXES FOR {{EVERYDAY ACHES}} NOBODY TAUGHT YOU
facts: **Hiccups** – Swallow a teaspoon of sugar; it resets the nerve signal that's causing the spasm.
**Sore Throat** – Gargle warm water with half a teaspoon of salt for 30 seconds, a few times a day.
**Stuffy Nose** – Hold a warm, damp washcloth over your sinuses for a few minutes to loosen congestion.
**Burnt Tongue** – Press a spoonful of plain yogurt or honey against the roof of your mouth to cool it fast.
**Toothache** – Press a small ice cube into the webbing between your thumb and index finger for a few minutes.
**Bad Breath Fast** – Chew a sprig of raw parsley; its chlorophyll neutralizes odor-causing compounds.
**Charley Horse Cramp** – Pinch your upper lip firmly for 20-30 seconds to interrupt the muscle spasm signal.
**Eye Twitch** – Press a cold spoon gently against the eyelid for a minute to calm the overactive nerve.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
A few of these old-school tricks actually hold up under the science. The hiccup fix with **sugar** works because the granules stimulate the vagus nerve in your throat, which helps override the misfiring signal between your diaphragm and brain. For a **sore throat**, warm salt water pulls excess fluid out of inflamed throat tissue through osmosis, which reduces swelling and temporarily eases the pain and that scratchy feeling. And the **charley horse** lip pinch isn't just a weird old wives' tale — pressing on that nerve-dense spot sends a competing signal to your brain that can interrupt the muscle spasm cycle long enough for the cramp to release. Everyone's body responds a little differently, so take these as a starting point, not a guarantee.
